title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
description: Ten named destinations along Hayward corridors, each paired with one documented reason to stop.

cards.title: Downtown Library for Study Resources
cards.subtitle: C Street corridor · Downtown Hayward
cards.notes: Head to the C Street block when you need public library collections, educational resources, or a change of study setting.
cards.short_summary: A civic learning stop centered on the downtown library.
cards.evidence_claim: Hayward Public Library identifies its Downtown Library at 888 C Street and says the library supports personal and educational growth through programming and resources.
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s current hours page before leaving; operating hours changed effective January 1, 2026.

cards.title: Heritage Plaza for Public Art
cards.subtitle: C Street and Watkins Street corridor · Downtown Hayward
cards.notes: Walk the C Street edge and follow the interpretive signs and artworks documenting communities and events in Hayward history.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor civic plaza where art interprets local history.
cards.evidence_claim: The City says Heritage Plaza includes interpretive signs and artworks about Hayward’s cultural histories, plus an arboretum walk with labeled trees.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public plaza; consult the City calendar for events that may affect use of gathering areas.

cards.title: City Hall for Civic Participation
cards.subtitle: B Street corridor · Downtown Hayward
cards.notes: Use the B Street block to attend a posted public meeting or reach the appropriate city office for an in-person service.
cards.short_summary: A downtown stop for local government services and meetings.
cards.evidence_claim: Hayward City Hall is at 777 B Street; the City’s visitor page describes on-site departments and services, while its government page documents public council meetings there.
cards.access_notes: Verify the relevant office or meeting schedule before visiting; free public parking is listed in the Watkins Street Garage.

cards.title: Sun Gallery for Local Exhibitions
cards.subtitle: E Street corridor · Downtown Hayward
cards.notes: Plan an E Street stop during posted gallery hours to see visual-art exhibitions reflecting Hayward-area communities.
cards.short_summary: A community gallery with rotating visual-art programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Sun Gallery is located at 1015 E Street and presents visual-art exhibitions and educational programs; its official page states gallery visits are free.
cards.access_notes: The official page lists Friday and Saturday hours of 11 a.m.–4 p.m.; confirm before traveling.

cards.title: Japanese Gardens for a Path Walk
cards.subtitle: North Third Street corridor at Crescent Avenue
cards.notes: Follow the designated garden paths from North Third Street, keeping food and drinks outside to preserve the quiet setting.
cards.short_summary: A landscaped garden stop governed by clear visitor rules.
cards.evidence_claim: H.A.R.D. lists Japanese Gardens at 22373 North Third Street and documents daily public hours, designated paths, and restrictions on food and beverages.
cards.access_notes: Listed public hours are 8:30 a.m.–4 p.m. daily, with specified holiday closures; remain on paths or gravel areas.

cards.title: HAHS Museum for Local History
cards.subtitle: Foothill Boulevard corridor · Downtown Hayward
cards.notes: Take the Foothill Boulevard block to compare the history and art galleries, then contact the archivist separately for research.
cards.short_summary: A second-floor museum focused on Hayward-area stories.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hayward Area Historical Society places its Museum of History & Culture at 22380 Foothill Boulevard and identifies both a History Gallery and HAHS Art Gallery.
cards.access_notes: The galleries list Thursday–Saturday hours, 11 a.m.–3 p.m.; the museum is on the accessible second floor.

cards.title: Sulphur Creek for Wildlife Education
cards.subtitle: D Street corridor · Hayward Hills
cards.notes: Follow D Street to view resident wildlife and the Discovery Center; call first if your purpose is an injured-animal intake.
cards.short_summary: A wildlife education and rehabilitation center near campus.
cards.evidence_claim: H.A.R.D. identifies Sulphur Creek Nature Center at 1801 D Street as a wildlife education and rehabilitation facility with animal displays and a discovery center; admission and parking are free.
cards.access_notes: Listed public hours are Tuesday–Sunday, 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; Monday is closed. Contact staff before bringing wildlife.

cards.title: Douglas Morrisson Theatre for Live Performance
cards.subtitle: North Third Street corridor · Near the Japanese Gardens
cards.notes: Pair this North Third Street stop with a scheduled production, checking the official season listing before choosing a date.
cards.short_summary: A community performing-arts venue on the garden corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: H.A.R.D. locates Douglas Morrisson Theatre at 22311 North Third Street and documents a performance series featuring local, national, and international talent.
cards.access_notes: Entry depends on the scheduled production; consult the official calendar and ticket listing before visiting.

cards.title: Meek Estate Park for Historic Grounds
cards.subtitle: Hampton Road corridor · Cherryland
cards.notes: Enter from Hampton Road to see the historic-building setting, lawn, picnic areas, and playground during park hours.
cards.short_summary: Historic estate grounds combined with everyday park amenities.
cards.evidence_claim: H.A.R.D. lists Meek Estate Park at 240 Hampton Road and documents a historical building, open lawn, picnic areas, playground, and restrooms.
cards.access_notes: The park is documented as open daily from sunrise to sunset; rentals require separate arrangements.

cards.title: Shoreline Center for Bay Ecology
cards.subtitle: Breakwater Avenue corridor · Hayward shoreline
cards.notes: Take Breakwater Avenue to the exhibits, then stay on designated shoreline trails to limit disturbance to feeding and nesting wildlife.
cards.short_summary: An interpretive gateway to the San Francisco Bay estuary.
cards.evidence_claim: H.A.R.D. locates the center at 4901 Breakwater Avenue and describes its exhibits and programs as an introduction to San Francisco Bay Estuary ecology.
cards.access_notes: The official nature-center page lists shoreline trails from dawn to dusk and limited interpretive-center days; verify current hours.
